# Long-term experience needs storage, utility, and admission checks

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/memory-and-skills.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-26 · 67 topic entries / 18 representative comparisons

MemGPT decides where information lives, MemPrice allocates fidelity within a limited window, and CMP studies how to identify utility. Voyager turns successful programs into skills, VaG manages admission risk, and SkillRise tests curation on later tasks. Fit, relevance, legitimacy, and future usefulness are four different questions. EMMA assigns structured memory to controller, agent, and skill, limiting each edit by failure scope and requiring actual use in the next attempt.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Allocation needs utility but does not create causal evidence

MemGPT moves information to archives, and MemPrice allocates representation levels within the window. Both need a keep decision. CMP studies identification instead: a memory retrieved disproportionately on difficult questions cannot be blamed for associated failures without randomized controls. When feeding CMP estimates into allocation, retain exposure design and uncertainty; net effects under fixed slots are not freely additive item values.

Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](../../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en.md)

### Current success, durable admission, and future usefulness happen at different times

Voyager accumulates successful programs as skills. VaG considers effects on descendants, checking before write-back and assessing compatibility in use. SkillRise scores curation from downstream outcomes: current success mainly evaluates solving, not whether documentation helps later. These are different evidence contracts, not a ranking. Record execution, admission, and cross-task learning separately.

Sources: [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md) · [When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en.md) · [SkillRise](../../../../agent-research/2607.26784-skillrise/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

DiscernMem separates wrong memory scope from content defects. Pair single-memory and no-memory replays under the same task, seed, and configuration, then check repairs against both parent-memory and no-memory references. This constrains simple reflection append: poor team results cannot be blamed on one memory, and a new version cannot inherit old measured effects. Local work covers measurement and version contracts, not LLM repair or replay.

Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Identify which entry to change, then show the change helps

DiscernMem uses isolated injection and paired no-memory replay to distinguish scope from defects and gates repairs against parent-memory and no-memory references. EMMA organizes editing by controller, agent specialization, and skill ownership; each reflection edits only one responsible entry, while execution slips affect only the temporary plan. One measures attribution and repair; the other limits the edit layer and how it must be exercised. Structural legality is not paired benefit, and an external semantic-safety Boolean is not an implemented LLM review.

Sources: [EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis](../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Omitting a record from the current window does not prove the weights can replace it

MemPrice chooses which representations to read under a budget and utility estimate. After an external training update, ENGRAM compares a retrieval-free candidate with Base+ETG on the same probes to decide which training records may leave retrieval. The first saves window space without showing that the weights have learned the skill; the second tests local behavior without establishing end-to-end capability or total storage savings.

Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation](../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en.md)

### Finding a relevant record and checking a lesson's source are different problems

MemFit preserves raw turns and uses summary indexing and hybrid retrieval to narrow candidates. WikiTrace links insights to interpretations and raw execution so a model can inspect why a lesson holds. Correct ranking cannot repair a false explanation; complete sources do not guarantee descent. Both local implementations are independent components: MemFit calls neither embeddings nor a cross-encoder, while WikiTrace calls neither a compiler LLM nor a test actor. Interface checks do not establish long-term question-answering gains.

Sources: [Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14320-wikitrace/README-en.md) · [MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory](../../../../agent-research/2610.00872-memfit/README-en.md)

### Worth allocating memory and supported by enough evidence are separate axes

MemPrice jointly assigns fidelity levels under token limits using utility and long-run pressure. LiSA asks whether retrieved broad rules have enough evidence, while retaining narrow conflict cues. Cheap memory need not be reliable; reliable memory need not be budget-optimal. Both rely on external semantic inputs, so exact synthetic-input computations are not task-capability gains.

Sources: [LiSA: Lifelong Safety Adaptation via Conservative Policy Induction](../../../../agent-research/2605.14454-lisa/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

### Remembering more and trusting authorization rules are separate problems

MemGPT makes long-term information retrievable through tiers. PolicyBank revises interpretations instead of repeatedly following flawed rules. Header selection reduces context but needs a real actor. Typed changes and provenance do not make an external PolicyAgent's update true; malicious feedback, permission review and formal validation remain external.

Sources: [PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2604.15505-policybank/README-en.md) · [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md)

### Memory price, value and credit require distinct measurement contracts

MemPrice trades externally estimated utility against token size under a hard budget, adapting long-run retention through a pressure queue. CoReMem requires future tasks from an identical inherited repository, a success-first reward and anchor-based traceability. Neither local kernel fills in external semantic models: fewer tokens do not imply fewer actions, and an anchor is not causality.

Sources: [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

### clam-memory: distinguish mechanism from capability

Read uses nine Perceiver cross-attention blocks with eight latent slots, each reading only session tokens. Carry applies one eight-head slot self-attention block, then one sigmoid gate per slot mixes oldQ with newx and LayerNorm stabilizes it. Decode uses one query per layer/rank pair to produce fixed rank-eight adapters plus a learned fixed bias. Adapter size does not grow with sessions; mean pooling is not a substitute. CoReMem values memory by future same-repository with/without-memory replay and trains provenance credit. CLAM distills full-history teacher behavior into weights. Prospective utility and a parametric memory channel are different; neither is validated by static summary similarity. Full experiment not reproduced due to cost(reviewDONE).

Sources: [Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs](../../../../agent-research/2611.20759-clam-memory/README-en.md) · [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md)

### Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

Search returns oldest matches under original record headers and line numbers:10 by default, at most30, with an offset over matching lines rather than records and up to three context lines. Prior grep outputs remain logged but are skipped by searches to avoid recursive duplication. Responses cap at6K characters, clip lines around matches to300 characters, stop at whole matches and return a continuation offset. Invalid regexes and searches exceeding ten seconds return errors. Controls check omitted summary details remain in the log, grep outputs do not duplicate original matches, case-insensitive search and continuation offsets work, and long lines/many hits respect6K. Catastrophic regex backtracking terminates only the worker and a later normal query still works. Model-turn budgets, token estimation and forced-answer calls are outside this storage/tool slice; no automatic compression policy or training gain is fabricated.

Sources: [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md) · [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md)

### MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management

Entity weights are log(N/df), so an entity common to every record can have zero weight. Shared entity mass and both signal variances adaptively mix weighted Jaccard with cosine. Variances are computed over every earlier/later pair in the W-window before positive-gain filtering and the d-edge-per-successor cap. Gain is measured against the successor's initial-anchor cosine. Hungarian matching maximizes total gain with at most one incoming and outgoing edge, and no incoming anchor edge. Thus links form forward nonbranching chains: anchored chains stay together, anchor-free chains choose the maximum summed cosine group, and unmatched records retain their initial group. Controls assign every record once,preserve K nonempty groups under duplicate embeddings,handle N1,reduce to cosine for universally common entities,and estimate window variance before filtering. Links must point forward,avoid incoming anchor edges and be nonbranching. A supplied-matrix unit test distinguishes greedy gain0.9 from Hungarian gain1.6; it is not memory accuracy. Verification can misjudge source facts, and the paper's fallback may choose a shorter candidate missing required facts, so ContextFolder must not be described as lossless storage.

Sources: [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md) · [MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging](../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en.md)

### MemLife: Curating and Reasoning over Long-Term Egocentric Video Memories

Eq.11 averages response tokens within each candidate before macro-averaging candidates,preventing long memories from dominating the baseline. Variance macro-averages token deviations around the same group mean,not each candidate's own mean; the latter would discard between-candidate informativeness/retrievability signal. Eq.12 normalization is clipped to plus/minus3,then response-token-recentered within each group,and finally globally mask-whitened. Prompt/padding positions stay excluded. KL is an Eq.16 loss term,not part of FIRM or advantage statistics. Training QA may construct training rewards,but the question-independent writer and evaluated reader cannot read test answers. Unequal-length candidates distinguish a macro mean.5 from pooled-token mean.25,and group variance.25 from zero within-candidate variance. Sparse outliers check post-clip recentering. Valid response rewards are restricted to[0,1];extreme finite padding is erased before arithmetic,and overflow from finite ratios times advantages or KL terms is rejected rather than returning infinity or disguising an overflowed variance as zero advantage. Further controls cover flat groups,empty candidates/padding,invalid probabilities,KL affecting only the separate loss,and future/other-subject entries excluded before ranking while exact-cutoff entries remain available. Inputs are explicit synthetic controls,no gold QA or video is passed to a reader,and pass rates are not video-QA capability.

Sources: [MemLife: Curating and Reasoning over Long-Term Egocentric Video Memories](../../../../agent-research/2609.40195-memlife/README-en.md) · [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md)

### Retained evidence and abstract lessons do not validate each other

DualPM local polarity is not an episode label. Two episode-model calls precede separate polarity maintenance. Frozen blocks prevent early within-block exposure, while lineage remains model-claimed rather than semantically verified. GrepMem logs/paginated grep can recover omitted text without establishing correct model retrieval or use. DualPM rules may transfer or overgeneralize. Controlled callbacks establish only L0 immutability/atomic contracts, not L1 memory policy or success rates. The full API campaign is terminally not reproduced for cost.

Sources: [Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory](../../../../agent-research/2611.33612-dualpm/README-en.md) · [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If MemPrice selects a high-utility memory, why does CMP ask how utility was measured? {#cross-allocation-versus-identification}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Knapsack optimizes supplied utilities and sizes, not their reliability. Low success on tasks that often retrieve a memory can reflect selection bias. CMP uses balanced randomized exposure and controls to estimate net effect with a standard error. Slot substitution affects the result, so it cannot become an independent additive knapsack value unconditionally.

    **Illustrative example:** A troubleshooting memory is retrieved for the hardest incidents. Determine what happens without it before interpreting low success or budgeting window space.

    Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](../../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en.md)

### Why can't a Voyager program that succeeded once enter VaG's long-term library unchecked alongside all other skills? {#cross-successful-skill-versus-admission}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** One execution supports that path under its environment, not harmlessness under other prerequisites or compatibility with existing skills. VaG checks structure, behavior, and semantics before writing, then chooses compatible sets by marginal value. Success, harmlessness, and combined benefits remain separate gates.

    **Illustrative example:** A skill works in an empty directory but implicitly deletes old files. The original success does not validate a shared directory.

    Sources: [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md) · [When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en.md)

### Why can't SkillRise use Voyager-style current success to reward curation directly? {#cross-current-outcome-versus-future-skill}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Current success measures actions just taken; a document's utility emerges on later related tasks. SkillRise separates solve and curate phases and applies discounted downstream returns to the latter's generated tokens. Successful program admission does not supply this cross-task credit. A polished but unhelpful summary should not be rewarded automatically.

    **Illustrative example:** A solver can succeed by luck but record only the answer. Downstream evaluation reveals the lack of reusable steps.

    Sources: [SkillRise](../../../../agent-research/2607.26784-skillrise/README-en.md) · [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md)

### Why might a repaired memory that beats its parent still be rejected? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The parent can be harmful. A candidate must also match or beat no-memory, retain historical task performance, and not increase complete failures. One positive difference does not satisfy both non-regression references.

    **Illustrative example:** Parent memory scores 0.2, the repair 0.4, and no memory 0.8. Beating the parent does not establish usefulness.

    Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Does EMMA's one-entry edit satisfy DiscernMem's causal attribution and repair checks? {#cross-emma-single-edit-versus-memory-effect}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Single edits limit scope and clarify responsibility but still need actual exercise and rerun. DiscernMem separately uses paired isolated memory and no-memory results on matching tasks and seeds, then checks that the candidate is no worse than both parent and no-memory. Structure and effect have different acceptance conditions.

    **Illustrative example:** Writing a transient retrieval typo into a permanent skill violates EMMA scope. Correcting the skill text does not prove that memory helps more than omitting it.

    Sources: [EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis](../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### If MemPrice omits a record this round, can that signal directly approve ENGRAM memory release? {#cross-engram-approval-versus-window-budget}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MemPrice allocates representations under a budget. ENGRAM also needs current training participation, reserved probes, and a retrieval-free candidate that clears both thresholds. An archived record is not deleted from physical storage.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Two correct answers out of four require retention at a strict 50% floor, even when Base+ETG got only one correct.

    Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation](../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en.md)

### If the most relevant lesson already ranks first, why does WikiTrace still need raw traces, and what does MemFit's retrieval test establish? {#cross-source-link-versus-memory-ranking}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Relevance determines what appears first, not whether a lesson is true or applicable. WikiTrace permits inspection of observations omitted by a summary. MemFit's local fusion hook checks externally supplied score composition, not model-computed semantic relevance or descent. Source fidelity, ranking and actual use need separate validation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a lesson says the task ended, but the raw trace contains a later submission. Ranking first does not fix the omission; a correct link does not establish the model notices it.

    Sources: [Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14320-wikitrace/README-en.md) · [MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory](../../../../agent-research/2610.00872-memfit/README-en.md)

### A short rule fits MemPrice's budget after one supporting observation. Why might LiSA still withhold it? {#cross-cross-memory-confidence-versus-capacity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Capacity allocation and evidential reliability are distinct. A candidate's cost and utility can justify its representation without proving correctness. Beta(2,1)'s 5% quantile is about 0.22361, below 0.55. A narrow observed conflict cue instead follows the local channel's different rule.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: retain a ten-token rule in storage, but delay using it as general safety advice after only one success; separately surface public/private contextual boundary cues.

    Sources: [LiSA: Lifelong Safety Adaptation via Conservative Policy Induction](../../../../agent-research/2605.14454-lisa/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

### Can successful workflow memory replace PolicyBank's authorization updates? {#cross-cross-colm-policybank}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not necessarily. Past trajectories may repeatedly follow a flawed spec. PolicyBank targets authorization deltas in developer feedback; local storage still lacks semantic repair.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: ten successful rebookings do not settle compensation without rebooking.

    Sources: [PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2604.15505-policybank/README-en.md) · [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md)

### Must lower memory-token occupancy increase CoReMem prospective value? {#cross-cross-nov15-coremem}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Compression may remove a needed future check. CoReMem measures later resolution/work from identical inherited states; MemPrice capacity and this reward are not interchangeable.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: removing a short test command saves a few tokens but may add ten exploration steps.

    Sources: [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

### How does CLAM differ from CoReMem? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-clam-memory}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** CLAM distills full-history answers into parameters. CoReMem uses future-task with/without-memory value for credit. Neither is a cheap stand-in for the other.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: retaining a name does not prove fewer steps on the next repository task.

    Sources: [Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs](../../../../agent-research/2611.20759-clam-memory/README-en.md) · [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md)

### How does its memory differ from MemGPT? {#cross-cross-nov20-grepmem}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** MemGPT manages layers and paging; GrepMem preserves raw text and retrieves through regex without a semantic index. Neither storage unit test proves model recall.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: grepping an order ID needs no prior extraction into a structured memory entry.

    Sources: [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md) · [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md)

### Can MemFolder's temporal chains replace MemForest's event trees? {#cross-cross-nov21-memfolder}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MemFolder permits at most one incoming/outgoing edge and reassigns anchor-free chains together. MemForest preserves event-tree hierarchy and retrieves through anchor neighborhoods.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a parent event with two child events fits a tree but not a nonbranching matched chain.

    Sources: [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md) · [MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging](../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en.md)

### Do MemOpt and MemFolder optimize the same object? {#cross-cross-nov21-memlife}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MemOpt decomposes training rewards to improve writer outputs;MemFolder organizes and compresses existing records. Fewer retrieval units do not prove greater faithfulness or fact retention.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: grouping two records changes structure;lowering credit for a hallucinated token optimizes the writer.

    Sources: [MemLife: Curating and Reasoning over Long-Term Egocentric Video Memories](../../../../agent-research/2609.40195-memlife/README-en.md) · [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md)

### Is bounded DualPM more lossless than GrepMem? {#cross-cross-nov26-dualpm}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They target different things. GrepMem retains raw trajectories for grep; DualPM abstracts transferable procedural lessons and may discard detail. Bounded memory guarantees neither detail recovery nor lesson utility.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an order number may remain in GrepMem's log while DualPM retains only the procedure to resolve an order ID before acting.

    Sources: [Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory](../../../../agent-research/2611.33612-dualpm/README-en.md) · [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-26** · DualPM local polarity is not an episode label. Two episode-model calls precede separate polarity maintenance. Frozen blocks prevent early within-block exposure, while lineage remains model-claimed rather than semantically verified. GrepMem logs/paginated grep can recover omitted text without establishing correct model retrieval or use. DualPM rules may transfer or overgeneralize. Controlled callbacks establish only L0 immutability/atomic contracts, not L1 memory policy or success rates. The full API campaign is terminally not reproduced for cost. Review DONE; no full campaign, automatic retry or Evolve promotion.

Affected: [Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory](../../../../agent-research/2611.33612-dualpm/README-en.md) · [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md)

**2026-11-21** · The local slice takes explicit probability/reward arrays and response masks for the Eq.7 margin,FIRM product,Eq.11-12 macro statistics,clipping/group-token recentering/global whitening,and Eq.16 scalar loss from supplied ratios,advantages and KL. An independently derived NumPy float64 protocol uses normalization epsilon1e-6,whitening epsilon1e-8 and sample-variance correction1; bitwise trainer equivalence is not claimed. Empty candidates are excluded fromG,empty groups output zero,and fewer than two valid batch tokens are rejected. Bounded unit-vector SearchMemory/FetchMemory first filter full interval containment and end<=query_time,then rank and return chronologically. Single-subject filtering is a local isolation contract,not the paper's mixed-subject LVQA benchmark or caller authentication. No video/embedding model,VLM judge,writer/reader,training-data construction,cached-reader trace collection,RL trainer or Evolve integration is implemented. Full experiments are not reproduced.

Affected: [MemLife: Curating and Reasoning over Long-Term Egocentric Video Memories](../../../../agent-research/2609.40195-memlife/README-en.md) · [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md)

**2026-11-21** · The local RecordFolder grouping kernel consumes explicit embeddings and grounded entity sets: normalization, DPC/novelty anchors, full-window variances, IDF affinity, positive-gain candidates, actual SciPy Hungarian matching and chain reassignment. Inputs must be chronological and contain at most512 records. Population variance with ddof0,Python rounding,input-order ties and anchors pinned to their own groups under duplicate embeddings are explicit deterministic conventions where the paper leaves details open. There is no LLM entity extraction, alias merging,text consolidation,ContextFolder,embedding model or downstream QA. Callers supply grounded labels and chronological order; lexical Jaccard is not substituted for semantic embeddings. No paths or Codex conversations are read, and no user files are automatically removed or compressed. Full experiments are not reproduced.

Affected: [MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management](../../../../agent-research/2611.26427-memfolder/README-en.md) · [MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging](../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en.md)

**2026-11-20** · The local substrate implements append-only records, explicit-summary compaction, post-compaction grep admission, regex/pagination/context/original line numbers, recursive-output exclusion and character limits. Regexes run in a separate worker with a hard timeout over supplied text, never paths. Summaries are explicit caller inputs. There is no LLM summarizer, GRPO, question answering or real-history integration. Tests use synthetic public observations and never read local Codex sessions; string retrieval is not agent capability. Full experiments not reproduced.

Affected: [Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.25123-grepmem/README-en.md) · [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · This is review-only: no executable adapter, metrics or GPU receipt, and no weight/corpus downloads. The record preserves read/carry/decode, two-stage training, rank and retrieval protocols. A forward pass through an untrained random hypernetwork would not reproduce consolidation capability. Full campaign not reproduced; no capability claim.

Affected: [Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs](../../../../agent-research/2611.20759-clam-memory/README-en.md) · [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md)

MemPrice allocates context capacity/fidelity; CoReMem optimizes future resolution/work. Token occupancy, action steps and semantic utility differ, and local kernels generate no memory.

Affected: [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](../../../../agent-research/2611.17316-coremem/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

**2026-10-29** · DiscernMem separates wrong memory scope from content defects. Pair single-memory and no-memory replays under the same task, seed, and configuration, then check repairs against both parent-memory and no-memory references. This constrains simple reflection append: poor team results cannot be blamed on one memory, and a new version cannot inherit old measured effects. Local work covers measurement and version contracts, not LLM repair or replay.
